missionPremise: Dispatch 2026-09-09_ctx-prov: McLennan 48309:103671 is the only failure left on an otherwise-clean staging walk (pass=181, fail=1, BP-CONFORMANT-01, three consecutive runs unchanged). The retired planner's own unverified-claims section flagged and then retracted an inference that this matches Caldwell 48055:1's roll-dropout class, on the correct ground that McLennan has only one CAD vintage and cannot have a roll-dropout population. This lane starts from nothing rather than inheriting that retracted inference, per explicit instruction.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this done by: (1) the rule BP-CONFORMANT-01 actually enforces is written down, verified against its own source, and now lives as a comment on responseCarriesConformantV1 (previously undocumented anywhere); (2) 48309:103671's served payload is quoted verbatim and read against that rule, naming which check it fails and why; (3) a mechanism is named with source-level evidence (not inference from the dispatch's prose or from a sibling lane's prose) and at least one candidate is explicitly rejected with evidence; (4) the failing population is counted for all six counties with its counting rule stated inline, not just for McLennan; (5) no fix was made in hauska-factory beyond documentation, because the diagnosed defect lives in legacy-design-tools, which the dispatch forbids writing to -- and the report is precise enough that a dispatch can be compiled against that repo without a second diagnostic pass; (6) the concurrent CTX-WALKRULE lane's uncommitted edits in the same file were checked for actual line overlap, not just file-level proximity.
scopeBasis: In scope: reading the rule and the served payload (both explicitly permitted, HTTP reads are 'not an execution'); establishing mechanism and population via read-only queries against the STAGING Neon store (matching the target the recorded walk actually used) with credentials pulled from gcloud Secret Manager and deleted immediately after use, mirroring the read-only pattern already established in scripts/ctx-w2/*.mjs; documenting the true predicate in verify-walk.mjs as a comment (dispatch step 1 explicitly asks for this to be 'written down', calling it half the lane's value). Out of scope, deliberately: any change to legacy-design-tools (nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts, where the actual defect lives), any change to hauska-engine or hauska-map, any deploy/Cloud Build/job execution/bake/publish/walk run, any change to cloudbuild.publish.yaml's _LDT_SHA pin, and any change to BP-CONFORMANT-01's pass/fail logic itself (the rule is not wrong -- the data genuinely is non-conformant for the affected rows -- so 'do not widen the predicate' was honored by leaving the logic untouched).

step1_provenanceRuleWrittenOut.whatItChecksPerLayer: It does NOT check per layer, despite the failure reason text ('facets lack conformant-v1 provenance per layer') and the file's header comment implying a layer-by-layer audit. responseCarriesConformantV1(body) is two whole-body checks: (1) FAIL immediately if body.facets.facetSchemaVersion === 'node-facets-tier1-v1' (OLD_TIER1_FACET_SCHEMA_VERSION, the old-shape literal); (2) otherwise PASS iff JSON.stringify(body) contains the substring 'conformant-v1' anywhere at all. This is now written as a comment directly above the function (src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs), which previously had only a one-line comment and no explanation of the actual mechanics.
step1_provenanceRuleWrittenOut.whatShapeSatisfiesIt: In practice, a row's facetSchemaVersion being exactly 'node-facets-tier1-conformant-v1' (TIER1_CONFORMANT_FACET_SCHEMA_VERSION) is sufficient on its own, since that string contains the substring 'conformant-v1'. provenance.parcelSource carrying the bake's 'conformant-v1-cad-parcel-roll' literal would independently satisfy it too. The finer, leaf-by-leaf provenance audit is a separate check, BP-CONTENT-01 (gradeTier1Content), which runs strictly after BP-CONFORMANT-01 and was not confused with it in this diagnosis.

step2_servedPayload.fetchedFrom: https://smart-site-factory.vercel.app/site/api/spine/cortex/api/brokerage/v1/place/node/48309:103671/facets (the exact URL pattern walkParcel builds), HTTP 200
step2_servedPayload.whichLayerFails: facetSchemaVersion (check 1, the old-shape literal exclusion) fails immediately; the walk never even reaches the substring check. facets.provenance carries the pre-conformant txgio parcelSource, not the CAD-roll-driven conformant source -- provenance is the layer that actually reveals the mechanism, even though the failing check itself is whole-body.
step2_servedPayload.noRecordRetirement: The payload carries no recordRetirement field anywhere -- confirms this is not a CTX-RETIRE roll-dropout case.

step3_mechanism.chosen: The conformant bake CLI (legacy-design-tools/artifacts/api-server/src/nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts, verified at origin/main 3885efad) permanently skips writing a row, on every run forever, when: the parcel's prop_id IS present in the current declared-vintage CAD roll (rollAbsent === false -- true for every row in this population, since none are retired) AND the CAD claim's raw situsAddress is punctuation-only. Source: situsForBake(body) calls assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly (serveGuards.ts: PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE = /^[\s,.\-;:'"`]+$/); when it throws, situsForBake returns {situs:null, refuse:true}; the per-row loop (lines ~336-345) does `if (rollAbsent) { situs = situsForRetiredBake(body) } else { const {situs:s, refuse:refuseSitus} = situsForBake(body); if (refuseSitus) { skippedBadSitus += 1; continue } situs = s }`. The `continue` fires BEFORE any DB write, so the row's snapshot is never touched -- it stays frozen on whatever schema/bakedAt it last held, indefinitely, across every subsequent bake run for that county.
evidenceFor: 100% match, not a sample, across all three affected counties: every failing row has a punctuation-only baseFacts.situsAddress (16104/16104 Bastrop, 768/768 Hays, 1165/1165 McLennan -- measured live via SQL regex against the exact same PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE pattern serveGuards.ts uses).

100% match: every failing row carries provenance.parcelSource = 'txgio' -- the pre-conformant bake's literal (nodeFacetTier1Assemble.ts's ParcelSource union is exactly 'txgio' | 'conformant-v1-cad-parcel-roll'; zero failing rows carry the latter).

bakedAt is frozen and disjoint from passing rows: Hays's 768 failing rows share exactly ONE bakedAt (2026-07-23T15:22:13.921Z); McLennan's 1,165 share exactly ONE bakedAt (2026-07-24T19:33:06.683Z, matching the served payload above bit-for-bit). Passing rows in the same counties were baked today, 2026-09-09, repeatedly (McLennan's passing bakedAt window is 16:27:28-16:39:36Z -- one second before the recorded failing walk 4c3d0746 completed at 16:39:51Z). The failing set has not moved across any bake run since its original bakedAt.

Read from source directly, not from a sibling lane's prose: CTX-RETIRE's PR #647 (legacy-design-tools, merged 2026-09-09T13:13:58Z as commit 3885efad -- the exact LDT_SHA this dispatch's publish image cloudbuild.publish.yaml is pinned to) added the rollAbsent branch (situsForRetiredBake, which has no punctuation guard) specifically for roll-absent accounts, and its own close artifact (_inbox/2026-09-09_ctx-retire_close.json) states rule3 of its own walk-grading proposal: 'BP-CONFORMANT-01 ... is UNCHANGED ... it is not a new tolerance, it is the walk's EXISTING rule finally being satisfiable for [the 63 roll-absent Caldwell accounts]'. Reading nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts at that exact merged commit confirms the `else` branch (on-roll accounts, situsForBake, skippedBadSitus) is untouched by that PR.
step3_mechanism.rejected: That this matches Caldwell 48055:1's class (a roll-dropout/retired account, per the retired planner's retracted inference). Rejected on: (1) the dispatch's own instruction -- McLennan has one CAD vintage, no roll-dropout population is possible; (2) live verification -- 48309:103671 carries no recordRetirement field and takes the bake CLI's on-roll (`else`) branch, not the rollAbsent branch; (3) Caldwell itself now measures 0/48,649 failures post-PR#647, confirming its roll-absent population is fixed and disjoint from this dispatch's still-open on-roll population. The two classes share one ROOT CODE PATH (situsForBake's punctuation guard) but are different POPULATIONS with different fixes: PR #647 already covers roll-absent accounts; the on-roll skip-before-write for a blank/placeholder CAD situs is untouched and is the actual cause of all 18,037 rows this dispatch found.
step3_mechanism.ruleNotWrong: BP-CONFORMANT-01 itself is not the defect. It correctly identifies that these 18,037 rows were never touched by the conformant bake -- that is a true statement about the data, not a false positive from an overbroad or malformed check. No change was made to its logic.

step4_population.countingRule: READ-ONLY, live, STAGING (STAGING_NEONDB_URL, gcloud Secret Manager, deleted after use -- matching the target smart-site-factory.vercel.app/site that produced the recorded walk 4c3d0746). Query: place_layer_snapshots WHERE place_key LIKE 'node:<fips>:%' AND adapter_key = 'node-facets:tier1'; FAIL := facetSchemaVersion = 'node-facets-tier1-v1' OR payload_json::text NOT LIKE '%conformant-v1%' -- the SAME predicate as responseCarriesConformantV1, re-expressed in SQL against the identical stored payload the serve route returns verbatim as body.facets (confirmed by comparing the live HTTP fetch to the SQL row for 48309:103671 -- exact match). Predicate control: the query matched 1,516,110 rows total across all six counties (not zero), ruling out a broken WHERE clause silently reporting a false absence, per the same control discipline scripts/ctx-w2/cadroll-served-state.mjs already established as this program's convention.

48055_Caldwell.note: CTX-RETIRE PR #647's roll-absent fix already resolved this county's population; disjoint from this dispatch's finding.

48309_McLennan.note: The dispatch-named parcel 48309:103671 is one of these 1,165, not an isolated case.

step4_population.verdict: One parcel is a curiosity; this is a class. 18,037 rows across three counties fail, with Bastrop alone at 20.7% of its entire served population -- a launch blocker by the dispatch's own stated standard, not a per-county rounding error. The sampler-bias caveat the dispatch raised (low prop_id bias making a single surfaced failure weak evidence of rarity) is moot here: this count is a full-table scan of the served store, not a sample.

step5_fixLocation.reasonNotFixedHere: The defect is entirely in legacy-design-tools/artifacts/api-server/src/nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts's per-row bake loop (the `else` branch at situsForBake/skippedBadSitus, roughly lines 336-345 at commit 3885efad), which this dispatch explicitly forbids writing to. BP-CONFORMANT-01 in hauska-factory is not wrong and was not changed.
step5_fixLocation.whatWasDoneHereInstead: Documented the actual BP-CONFORMANT-01 predicate as a comment on responseCarriesConformantV1 (src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs), per the dispatch's explicit ask that this definition 'does not exist in writing anywhere and producing it is half the value of this lane'. Left a read-only leave-behind instrument, scripts/ctx-prov/provenance-population.mjs, which reproduces the step-4 count against any target's Neon store and can be re-run after a legacy-design-tools fix lands to confirm the population clears.

precisionForACompiledDispatch.targetFunction: situsForBake / the per-row loop's `else` branch (on-roll accounts), specifically the `if (refuseSitus) { skippedBadSitus += 1; continue }` line
precisionForACompiledDispatch.problemStatement: An on-roll (non-retired) account whose CAD claim carries a punctuation-only situsAddress is silently skipped by the conformant bake forever, leaving it stuck on whatever pre-conformant snapshot it last held (facetSchemaVersion node-facets-tier1-v1, parcelSource txgio) with no declared state distinguishing it from a genuinely unbaked row. This is the same underlying data-quality symptom CTX-RETIRE's situsForRetiredBake handled for roll-absent accounts (PR #647), but for accounts that ARE on the current roll -- 18,037 of them across Bastrop/Hays/McLennan as of 2026-09-09, likely recurring in future bakes wherever a CAD roll's situs field is blank or placeholder-only.
precisionForACompiledDispatch.suggestedShape_notAnImplementation: An on-roll account with an unusable situs is not retired and must not be routed through situsForRetiredBake's recordRetirement branch (that would misrepresent it as a roll-dropout it is not). It needs its own declared state -- e.g. a situs-quality absence/refusal on the situs leaf, written WITH the row (not skipping the write) so the row still reaches facetSchemaVersion=conformant-v1 and carries an honest, four-state-compliant absence for situsAddress specifically, rather than the whole row vanishing from the bake's write path. This is a proposal for the receiving lane's own diagnosis, not a prescribed fix -- CTX-PROV did not design or implement it, per the dispatch's scope.
